D.treatment: real disinfectant scent added to VR headset

O.outcome_detail: hand disinfection immediately when leaving the patient environment

cells.quote: For final hand disinfection, defined as disinfection immediately when leaving the patient environment, a pronounced difference between groups was observed. Only 1 of 43 control participants (2.3%) exhibited this behavior, compared with 10 of 52 participants (19.2%) in the intervention group. Fisher exact test yielded an OR of 9.82 (95% CI 1.29-443.13; P=.01).
cells.note: Exploratory end point; the study states that the wide CI reflects the low event rate in the control group and warrants cautious interpretation.

D.treatment: real disinfectant scent added to VR simulation

O.outcome_detail: overall hand disinfection during the simulation

result.effect: OR=2.73, 95% CI 1.09-7.40; P=.04; absolute risk increase 19.9 percentage points; NNT=5

cells.quote: The olfactory intervention nearly tripled the odds of hand disinfection (8/43, 18.6% vs 20/52, 38.5%; an absolute risk increase of 19.9 percentage points; OR=2.73, 95% CI 1.09‐7.40; P=.04; number needed to treat=5).
cells.note: Participants were quasi-randomly allocated by preassigned room rather than individually randomized.

cells.note: Cross-sectional measured association; age was not a manipulated learning-design condition.

O.outcome_detail: 40-item nutritional-medicine knowledge test score

result.effect: mean difference: 2.4 points (95% CI [0.7, 4.0]); Cohen's d = 0.65; p = 0.004

cells.quote: The median test score was 30 points in the OLM group and 27 points in the IPL group (see Figure 2). Both the permutation Welch t-test and the Wilcoxon–Mann–Whitney test indicated a significant difference in test performance between groups, with students in the OLM group achieving higher scores. The mean difference was 2.4 points (95% CI [0.7, 4.0]; t = −2.89, p = 0.004), corresponding to a medium effect size (Cohen’s d = 0.65).
cells.note: The study states that students had sufficient prior knowledge in medicine to participate, but does not state their prior knowledge of nutritional medicine specifically.

cells.note: Grades were derived from the post-course 40-item knowledge test.

O.outcome_detail: perceived content delivery, overall course evaluation, and exam preparation

cells.quote: The perceived suitability of the course format for conveying the topics was higher in the OLM group compared with the IPL group. Students also provided higher overall ratings of the course format and the course itself when taught via the online module. A pronounced difference in means was observed for the adequacy of exam preparation, with higher ratings in the OLM group compared to the IPL group. Consistent with this, a greater proportion of students in the OLM group indicated openness to taking the same format again for exam preparation.
cells.note: The questionnaire was developed for internal evaluation purposes and was not formally validated.
